stage1.impression: A clean, legible bar interior with a strong graphic idea, the spectrum front, but it reads as an archviz render rather than a photograph. The light is flat and too bright for a night listening bar, the panels look like uniformly lit plastic sheets with clipped saturation, the back-bar is a field of cloned, denoiser-smeared bottles, and a bright wall and ceiling hotspots pull the eye away from the panels. The EARF speaker on the bar is a tiny red shape that reads as a toy.

blocking_9: Night mood: overall exposure down about 1 stop so the panels and shelves are the brightest things in the frame (frame lum_median under 60, panels 2x the surrounding wall)
Panels read as light passing through tinted cast acrylic: visible vertical gradient and a soft falloff, no single-channel clipping (green panel r_median currently 0)
No surface brighter than the panels: the blank wall right of the back-bar (lum 206) and the floor hotspot (12% clipped) brought under the panel level
Back-bar bottles that do not read as clones, with crisp labels and no denoiser smear
Even back-lit ceiling membrane with no blotchy hotspots
A foreground that leads into the spectrum, not a cut-off dark stool mass at the left edge

defects.what: plain wall right of the back-bar is the brightest large area in the frame (lum_median 206), competing with the panels
specular hotspot on the floor, 12% clipped, an unexplained bright blob in the lower right
ceiling membrane shows blotchy uneven bright patches that read as stains or render artefacts, 1.3% clipped

bar panels are flat, uniform emitters with saturated, clipped channels (green r=0, blue/violet b about 248); they read as LED signage, not tinted acrylic; brightness uneven (yellow 173, red 101, Smoke 77)
back-bar bottles are a small set of repeated models; labels are smeared by the denoiser into mush
foreground stool cut by the left edge forms a heavy dark mass with no purpose
Bell pendant cropped by the top-left corner
unreadable dark screen or frame shape at the left edge of the back-bar
the speaker on the bar is tiny and reads as a red toy horn; no light passing through it
record wall rendered as a flat repeated texture, reads as wallpaper
global: evenly lit, low contrast, no pools of light and dark; haze barely visible

changes.problem: The frame is too bright and even for a night bar, so the panels do not glow against their surroundings.

evidence.measured: lum_mean 91, only 30% of pixels below 40; floor lum_median 104

change.to: 0.0 (about -1.1 stop), then raise the bar panels per c2 to keep them bright

changes.expected: The room falls to a dark, calm field; panels and shelves stay luminous; floor around 50-60

changes.problem: The panels read as flat clipped LED sheets rather than light through tinted acrylic, and their brightness is uneven across the spectrum.

evidence.measured: green panel r_median 0, g 162; blue b 246, violet b 249; yellow lum 173 vs red 101 vs Smoke 77

change.from: 0.6, graded 0.6 at foot to 1.0 at top
change.to: 1.2 after the exposure drop, graded 0.35 at foot to 1.0 at top; per-panel trim so the luminance of red, violet and Smoke rises to within 25% of yellow (red x1.4, Smoke x1.8, yellow x0.85)

changes.expected: A visible vertical falloff on each panel, a deeper floor-level glow, no channel at 0 or 255 in a panel's median, a balanced spectrum

changes.problem: The blank wall to the right of the back-bar is the brightest area in the frame and steals the eye from the spectrum.

change.setting: Fog niches / back-bar back panel and the bar-top pinhole nearest the wall
change.from: Fog niches 0.05, back panel 0.07, pinholes 140 W
change.to: Fog niches 0.02, back panel 0.03; aim the last pinhole 15 deg off the wall or drop it to 70 W

changes.expected: The wall drops to a mid-grey well below the panels

changes.problem: A clipped specular hotspot on the floor in the lower right pulls the eye to an empty corner.

change.setting: floor material roughness (and the source it mirrors, the ceiling membrane patch)
change.to: honed concrete, roughness 0.45 with a fine-grain roughness map, so the panels still smear a coloured reflection but the hotspot spreads

changes.expected: No clipped floor; the panels' coloured reflections stay as soft streaks

changes.problem: The ceiling membrane is blotchy, with bright patches that read as stains or render faults.

evidence.measured: lum_range high, clip_pct 1.3 at the patches

change.setting: membrane emission (clock 'sunset') and the record-wall spots
change.to: 0.003, and record wall spots narrowed to cone 45 and aimed lower so they stop washing the membrane

changes.expected: An even, dim ceiling glow without patches

changes.problem: The back-bar bottles are cloned and their labels are smeared by the denoiser, which says 'render' at a glance.

evidence.measured: seen at 2x crop: the same five or six bottle shapes repeat; labels blur into flat patches

change.from: small repeated bottle set; 256 samples, denoise on
change.to: at least 20 distinct bottle models with random scale (0.9-1.1), rotation and fill level; 512 samples at the delivered 2400 x 1600 with denoise prefilter 'accurate' and albedo/normal passes

changes.expected: Bottles read as a real collection with legible label edges

changes.problem: The cut-off foreground stool is a heavy dark mass and the top-left corner crops a pendant, so the frame leaks at both left corners.

evidence.measured: near-black stool fills the bottom-left corner; pendant cropped at [0, 0, 160, 50]

change.to: position [1.6, 4.6, 1.05], target [7.0, 8.4, 0.75], 35 mm, so the first stool sits whole inside the frame and the pendant drops out above

changes.expected: The spectrum runs from the left edge into depth with a clean foreground; no cropped objects at the corners

changes.problem: The air carries no visible atmosphere, so there is no depth between the bar and the lounge.

evidence.measured: lounge and record wall as crisp and contrasty as the foreground

changes.expected: Soft glow around the pendants and a slight veiling of the lounge, which separates the planes

out_of_scope.request: Make the Atmosphere speaker on the bar read as tinted acrylic with light passing through it, rather than a small opaque red horn
out_of_scope.why: It is the speaker's material and form; fixed. It could be lit from behind with a spot, but at this scale it will not read regardless

out_of_scope.request: Replace the record wall's flat repeated texture with modelled sleeves
out_of_scope.why: The record wall is part of the room's design as proposed; its asset fidelity is a modelling task for the owner to approve
